When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward and attempt to lead the event.  She said when AMAZING GAZE and AUTOMATED showed superior pace in the early stages she was crossed by those runners approaching the 1400 Metres.  She said a short distance later when racing wide and without cover ON THE LASH raced ungenerously and got its head up.  When questioned if there was an opportunity to go forward and lead the event approaching the 1200 Metres when the pace was being run outside of standard time Apprentice Yuen agreed with the Stewards that in retrospect she had made an error of judgement in not urging her mount forward at that stage to avoid covering additional ground.  She was advised that in similar circumstances she would be expected to show better judgement than what she did on this occasion.  Trainer P C Ng confirmed the instructions issued and stated that, in his opinion, Apprentice Yuen should have allowed ON THE LASH to go forward after being crossed by AMAZING GAZE and AUTOMATED.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Jumped only fairly and then shortly after the start was checked when crowded.  Y L Chung stated that after being checked at the start his mount settled back in the field and failed to show sufficient pace in the early stages to hold a more forward position.  He said after entering the Home Straight his vision was impaired due to the kickback and after shifting to the inside of DAY DAY VICTORY near the 250 Metres he commenced to ride his mount along.  He added after improving quickly behind CAP LINER he was obliged to ride his mount in a cautious manner approaching the 100 Metres as his vision was still impaired and he was concerned he was positioned too close to CAP LINER.  He added after improving to the inside of CAP LINER near the 50 Metres SUPER RUBICK KID finished the race off well, however, he was not able to fully test his mount due to his restricted visibility.  Noted to have bled from the left nostril after the race.  An endoscopic examination confirmed the horse to be a bleeder.  Before being allowed to race again, SUPER RUBICK KID will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Shortly after the start was badly crowded between TOPSPIN KING and HAPPY SHOOTER which was taken out by ONE MAN SHOW (Apprentice P N Wong) which shifted out whilst being ridden along.  Whilst the Stewards accepted that Apprentice Wong had made some effort to straighten her mount, she was reprimanded and advised in similar circumstances she would be required to make a greater effort to prevent her mounts from shifting ground.  Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that near the 700 Metres her mount shifted out when racing ungenerously and made contact with CALIFORNIA BAY.  She said DAY DAY VICTORY was then not comfortable racing inside other horses for some distance thereafter.  She added that after the 500 Metres DAY DAY VICTORY shifted out when awkwardly placed close to CALIFORNIA BAY.  When questioned regarding her riding in the Home Straight Apprentice Yuen stated that after shifting to the outside of ONE MAN SHOW when that runner was giving ground, her intention was to continue to shift out to secure clear running.  She said due to the kickback her visibility was impaired and as she shifted to the outside of ONE MAN SHOW she became positioned close to LUCKY DOCTOR when DAY DAY VICTORY shifted out further than she had intended.  She said as a result she was obliged to steady to avoid LUCKY DOCTOR before then shifting to the inside of that runner near the 200 Metres where she was able to secure clear running.  Apprentice Yuen was reminded of her obligations to report to the Stewards anything that affects her ability to ride her mounts out and, whenever possible, she must ensure that she avails herself of runs when they present.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Shortly after the start shifted out, resulting in its rider having to correct her mount.   Near the 500 Metres was steadied to avoid PEJIBAYE (J Orman) which shifted in when not sufficiently clear.  J Orman was advised to exercise more care.  Apprentice P N Wong stated that after this incident her mount raced keenly which resulted in it improving to the inside of PEJIBAYE near the 900 Metres where she was then obliged to restrain her mount.  She said the instructions were to lead, however, her mount did not show sufficient pace in the early stages to do so and was crossed by PEJIBAYE.  She added ONE MAN SHOW did not travel well thereafter before giving ground in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to be a "roarer” and an endoscopic examination also showed a substantial amount of blood in its trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, ONE MAN SHOW will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.

Near the 800 Metres became unbalanced when bumped by INFINITE RESOLVE which shifted in before being corrected by its rider.  J Orman stated that the instructions were to ride the horse back in the field.  He said with the pace of the event being run outside of standard time MIGHTY MASTS raced keenly.  He said in the Home Straight the horse responded only fairly to his riding and although disadvantaged by the slow early pace he was still disappointed with the horse’s performance.  Trainer W Y So confirmed the instructions and agreed with the assessment offered by Jockey Orman in respect to the performance of the horse.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, MIGHTY MASTS will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.

Shifted in near the 800 Metres and bumped MIGHTY MASTS.  When questioned C L Chau stated that his instructions were to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages as INFINITE RESOLVE races best when held up for a finishing effort in the Home Straight.  He said in accordance with his instructions, in the early stages when positioned to the outside of PACKING ANGEL he elected to remain racing in that position where he was wide and without cover.  He said although he was aware the pace of the event was being run outside of standard time he was reluctant to allow his mount to improve forward as he was of the opinion this would be in contrast to his instructions issued.  He said for this reason he remained racing towards the rear of the field in a three wide position, however, in the Home Straight INFINITE RESOLVE was unable to run on due to its wide run and being unable to make up ground due to the  slow pace set in the early stages.  Trainer M Newnham confirmed the instructions but stated that, in his opinion, Jockey Chau should have shown initiative in the middle stages to allow INFINITE RESOLVE to stride forward to cross PACKING ANGEL.  After considering his explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Chau that he had made an error of judgement by not improving forward of PACKING ANGEL in the early stages to avoid racing wide and without cover.  He was advised that in similar circumstances he would be expected to show better judgement than what he did on this occasion.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  C L Chau (DREAMING TOGETHER) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that after the 400 Metres he shifted his mount to the outside of MORGAN SUCCESS when there was not sufficient room to do so, resulting in DREAMING TOGETHER making contact with TRINITY TREASURE, taking TRINITY TREASURE wider and then across the running of QUANTUM LEGEND, resulting in QUANTUM LEGEND blundering badly when contacted by TRINITY TREASURE.  C L Chau was suspended from riding in races for one Hong Kong raceday to be conducted on Wednesday, 15 July 2026 at Happy Valley.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his very good race riding record.
